stops.note: 'rearing, bringing up', from educare; Quintilian's Institutio Oratoria (c. AD 95) plans a child's education from the cradle
revived from Latin by Renaissance writers; Rabelais satirises old-fashioned schooling through the education of Gargantua (1534)
the Elementary Education Act of 1870 set up board schools across England and Wales

current_meaning: the process of receiving or giving systematic instruction
